transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Head of ML, Apellus), Taylor Nguyen (CTO, Apellus), Morgan Reyes (Sr ML Eng, Apellus)

--- Auto-generated summary (brief):
Apellus is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployment — main asks: very long context (50k-100k tokens), multilingual support for EN/FR/DE/JP, function/tool calling (DB lookups + vector search), and strict security (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Interested in benchmarking open models (Mistral, Llama variants, local LLMs) for latency and cost.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining. we, uh, we're super excited to talk through Apellus's use case today. quick intros?
[00:09] Jordan (Apellus): Jordan here, head of ML, I look after the retrieval and NLU stack. we've been proofing some long document workflows, so that's, that's the core ask.
[00:16] Taylor (Apellus): Taylor, CTO. i'm mostly here for the infra and security questions.
[00:20] Morgan (Apellus): Morgan, ml eng, i'll be running the POC if we move forward.
[00:25] Maya: Great, thanks. Samir's my solutions engineer, he'll dig into model perf and benchmarks. Samir, wanna say hi?
[00:31] Samir (Redwood SE): Yep hi. Samir Patel, infra/latency focus. i'll ask a few technical q's and we'll map models to their strengths.
[00:38] Jordan: Cool. to kick off
our main product ingests long RFPs and internal manuals, typical doc lengths 30k to 120k tokens. we need consistent context handling, and we also do multi-lingual support (EN/FR/DE/JP) for summarization and QA.
[00:52] Morgan: Also, we need tool-calling — our app triggers DB lookups and an internal python microservice for policy checks. so function calling support is critical.
[01:03] Taylor: Security-wise, we're evaluating hosted but need clarity on data residency, KMS integration, SOC2 attestations, and ability to run in our VPC or on-prem for some clients.
[01:12] Maya: That's helpful. high level, Redwood supports Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). For model selection, we usually map: open Llama-family variants or Mistral-like models for cost/perf, and larger proprietary ones for highest quality. but since you mentioned tool-calling and very long contexts, we should walk through tradeoffs.
[01:31] Samir: quick clarifying q — are you currently using a vector DB + retrieval? and what's your latency SLOs for user-facing flows versus batch jobs?
[01:39] Jordan: yes, Pinecone for vectors now, latency SLOs are 300-500ms for short queries; for long-doc summarization it's batch with ~2-5s preferred but for some interactive sessions we need under 1s per response where possible.
[01:52] Samir: ok, interesting. long-contexts (50k+) change the cost model and sometimes we recommend a hybrid: prefix caching + retrieval-augmented chunking to avoid re-sending full context each time. Redwood has KV cache options and prefix caching to reduce tokens.
[02:06] Morgan: can you explain prefix caching again? sometimes the docs use different terms.
[02:10] Samir: sure — prefix caching keeps the initial key/value cache for repeated prefixes so tokens don't have to be re-encoded on every request. it's more effective if your workflows repeat a lot of the same preamble. note: for arbitrarily long documents you'll still do chunk-based retrieval, but caching + batching lowers per-token cost and latency.
[02:28] Jordan: okay that makes sense. what about model choices for multilingual? we've seen mixed results with some open models.
[02:35] Samir: multilingual coverage varies — some Llama-based checkpoints do fine en-fr-de but Japanese is hit or miss; Mistral-family and certain instruction-tuned models handle multi-lang better. we can include a shortlist: Llama-3 variants, Mistral-instruct-xx, and some StarCoder-like models for code/tooling. we'll run language-specific evals.
[02:56] Taylor: and function calling — do open models support robust deterministic function calls or is that a managed layer?
[03:02] Maya: Redwood exposes function/tool calling as part of our API; when models don't natively support structured tool calling we overlay a small orchestration layer that parses and routes. for models with built-in function calling (some instruction-tuned ones) it's more seamless. we'll include examples.
[03:17] Morgan: i wanna talk latency — if we pick a bigger open model versus a quantized smaller one, how much difference are we seeing on dedicated GPUs?
[03:25] Samir: on dedicated A100-ish or H100-ish the big model can be 2-3x slower per token than a quantized 4-bit optimized variant but quality uplift may be noticeable for few-shot tasks. with Redwood Dedicated you can pick GPU type and we provide kernel selection and quantization profiles. for interactive sessions we often recommend mixing: smaller base for latency, fallback to larger for heavy-lift completions.
[03:48] Jordan: what's your approach to rolling out model variants? we have regulatory clients that restrict model families.
[03:53] Maya: rollout supports canary and A/B via the Console. you can pin models per route and set automatic fallback policies to cheaper variants if latency spikes or capacity hits. also audit logs track model/version usage.
[04:07] Taylor: about security — KMS integration: do you support customer-managed keys for Hosted? and for Private, is there full control?
[04:15] Samir: Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer KMS via bring-your-key patterns for certain tiers; Dedicated and Private let you bring full KMS/HSM and we integrate with cloud KMS providers. we'll send the KMS integration guide.
[04:27] Morgan: any SOC2 or ISO reports you can share? legal will want those before POC with real data.
[04:32] Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II report and our security pack are shareable under an NDA. we'll include that.
[04:38] Jordan: on data residency — some EU clients require data to stay in eu-west-1. can you pin regions?
[04:44] Samir: yes Hosted can pin region routing by policy, Dedicated pools can be deployed in specific cloud regions, and Private is fully under your network so data residency is under your control.
[04:54] Taylor: for the benchmark — we're thinking: 3 test cases: 1) 100k token summarization end-to-end (batch), 2) interactive QA with 50k context latency targets, 3) multilingual consistency across EN/FR/JP. how feasible is 100k?
[05:09] Samir: technically feasible if you chunk and use progressive summarization and KV streaming. some models are limited by context window, so we emulate extended contexts by retrieval + chained prompts. Redwood can orchestrate that and run a POC on Dedicated hardware to measure end-to-end latency and cost.
[05:26] Morgan: will the transcript include occasional ASR errors? (laugh) we get them in these calls often.
[05:30] Jordan: (laugh) yeah, please.
[05:34] Maya: (smiles) we'll keep things realistic.
[05:37] Jordan: any concerns about model hallucinations when doing tool-calling? we can't have incorrect DB updates.
[05:43] Samir: that's common, we recommend strict tool contracts — models should only return structured payloads and we add validation layers. for critical ops, run a shadow verify step or human-in-the-loop. Redwood supports routing outputs to validation functions before making state changes.
[05:58] Taylor: what about cost estimate for a 3-month POC with Dedicated? rough numbers ok.
[06:03] Maya: we'll provide a ballpark: Dedicated monthly commit for a small pool + per-token inference; we'll map scenarios (heavy long-context batch vs interactive). expect POC costs to be dominated by GPU hours for large-context tests. we'll send concrete examples.
[06:16] Morgan: any customers you've run similar long-context POCs with?
[06:20] Maya: yes, we've done long-doc summarization pilots with a legal-tech customer and a couple of enterprise search teams; we can anonymize benchmarks.
[06:29] Jordan: timeline — we hope a POC start mid-March and an evaluation period ~4 weeks. decisions by mid-April ideally.
[06:36] Maya: that aligns with our timelines. we'll aim to get you the pricing/security/benchmark plan within the week.
[06:42] Taylor: ok, last q: do you support private model hosting (bring-your-own model) behind Redwood Private? we might want to host custom fine-tuned checkpoints for compliance.
[06:52] Samir: yes, Private supports customer-managed models and we can load validated checkpoints in your VPC or on-prem; there are guidelines for model packaging and quantization.
[07:02] Jordan: perfect. next steps?
[07:05] Maya: recap — Redwood: send pricing examples, security pack (SOC2/KMS/SAML), SE benchmark plan for 100k context, recommended model shortlist. Apellus: share sample redacted prompts/data and confirm internal stakeholders for Private discussions. POC week of 2027-03-15 tentatively.
[07:25] Taylor: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:28] Morgan: thanks.
[07:30] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.
